task.prompt:
Please write a PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL procedure named `sp` with exactly this interface: `sp(arg1 integer, arg2 text, arg3 integer, arg4 integer, arg5 text, arg6 integer)`. The six inputs are, in order: manager age, manager work-start year, manager level, manager identifier, assignment from-year, and railway identifier.

Use the attached set of existing procedures in `components.sql`; call the component or components that fit the path, and don't recreate or modify them.

Before anything changes, remember the smallest railway identifier among management assignments whose from-year equals the fifth input. If nothing matches, remember null. Ordinary PostgreSQL equality applies, including nulls.

If that remembered identifier exists and the third input is strictly greater than 3, this is the high-level path: both components take part, and the railway picked by the sixth input has its construction year/value set to the third input. The component work in this path should reflect the requested manager, railway, and year values, plus the remembered earliest matching railway for the year cleanup.

Otherwise, run the alternate path: include the year cleanup component for the fifth input's year, using the railway number one higher than the sixth input as the cutoff. Also, if the third input is less than or equal to 3, remove management assignments for the fourth input's manager where the railway number is strictly below the sixth input. If not, remove management assignments for the sixth input's railway and the fifth input's from-year.

After the branch, if the second input isn't null, archive the matching manager profile's home country: same manager as the fourth input, same work-start year as the second input, country present, and not already beginning with exact 8-character prefix `archive_`; prefix the existing country with `archive_`.

Then use what's left. If that manager has no management assignments, prefix their non-null displayed name with exact 9-character prefix `inactive_`, unless it already starts that way. If that railway has no management assignments, prefix its non-null location with exact 11-character prefix `unassigned_`, unless it already starts that way. If that railway has no train records, prefix its non-null builder name with exact 9-character prefix `no_train_`, unless it already starts that way.

Don't add special null handling beyond the explicit checks above. Use normal PostgreSQL behavior for comparisons, text matching, concatenation, and assignments. Don't add custom exception handling; errors should bubble normally.

Return the complete stored procedure only, nothing else.
